tagline: Levee towns built for steamers, orchards and canneries.
intro: River Road leaves Courtland, beside the Sacramento River, for Walnut Grove and Isleton in the Delta. These were working towns. Courtland grew from a steamer landing opened in 1870, and the farms, orchards and canneries around them kept the main streets downriver in business.

Both downriver towns rebuilt their Asian business districts after fires. Walnut Grove's Japanese residents put up Kawashimo in 1916, two-story buildings with families living above their shops. Isleton rebuilt after 1926 in pressed-tin siding found in no other Asian community of the Delta.

moments.title: Courtland
moments.text: Courtland, named for a landowner's son, has held a Pear Fair for the Delta's Bartlett harvest since 1972.

moments.title: Walnut Grove Japanese-American Historic District
moments.text: Unlike other Japantowns in the area, Kawashimo was designed and built by its own Asian residents after the 1915 fire, some coming from as far as San Francisco.

moments.title: Isleton Chinese and Japanese Commercial Districts
moments.text: Isleton divided its two blocks of Main Street down the middle, Japanese American homes and businesses on one side and Chinese American on the other.
